meta.title: WHY TOURISTS ARE SKIPPING THAILAND FOR VIETNAM IN 2026–27
meta.description:
Why are so many tourists skipping Thailand in 2026 and 2027 and choosing Vietnam instead? Is Vietnam becoming the new Thailand?

After years of rising prices, changing visa rules, immigration restrictions, tourist fees, and complaints about scams and dual pricing, longtime Thailand visitors and expats are increasingly questioning whether the Land of Smiles is still worth it.

In this video, we compare Thailand vs. Vietnam, looking at tourism trends, cost of living, visa policies, safety concerns, and the growing popularity of destinations like Da Nang and Ho Chi Minh City. We also examine real experiences from longtime Thailand visitors who are now choosing Vietnam, and why Vietnam could eventually face some of the same problems.

What do you think? Is Thailand losing its appeal, or is Vietnam simply becoming a better alternative?** Share your experiences in the comments!

👍 Like this video, subscribe for more Thailand and Southeast Asia news, and share it with anyone planning a trip or considering retirement in Thailand or Vietnam.

comments.author: @yotoma
comments.text: Having cut my teeth living and working in Bangkok for 3 years during 1987-90, in addition to extensive travel in the country primarily during the late 90’s, I have the historic privilege of having enjoyed some of the best of the country. Having travelled in Vietnam during ‘95 and more recently ‘26, I see the trajectories and appreciate the differences. I however still find the Thai people very generous when you speak the language, which I suspect is similar in Vietnam. Prices higher but Thai food is much more to my liking, same with the women. I will continue to visit Thailand unlike my prior love affair with the Philippines.

comments.author: @sedoff1948
comments.text: I just arrived in Phu Quoc Island, Vietnam yesterday but didn’t realize one must fill out a pre-arrival form.  I was directed to a desk where a woman immigration staff helped me with kindness and smiles.  A year ago I arrived without sleep on a flight from Cairo to Bangkok.  I apparently didn’t fill out their digital form properly.  The immigration woman looked so annoyed with me and when I asked what I could do she dismissively, almost angrily, pointed to somewhere in the rear of the hall.  It was a computer but at 78 I still had a time filling out the form.   Fortunately, a woman at the information desk helped me out.  This is not a one time incident.  It’s happens with regularity. Like on the Express boat on the river, the guy handling the ropes or the woman taking the fares, they would snap at me for not following their protocol.  I’ve been to some 80 countries and actually grew up in Bangkok in the ‘50’s and I can’t recall so many unkindnesses as in Thailand.  I’m in Vietnam now and the people are far more cheerful and happy and look upon foreigners with curiosity and kindness a another fellow human being.  And last month in Egypt, never an unkindness, if one can ignore their bad behavior in traffic.

comments.author: @TimExpat
comments.text:
Every time Thais have a good business running with a bunch of foreigners, they ruined it eventually. They did it with the visa runs, easy way to get tourists to spend more time in Thailand. Then they did it with education visas. The language schools today are mostly empty and rotting away. Then they did it tourist visas with only limited number allowed of per year. Then next they ruined the DTL visas and remote workers. They are either moving back home or going to other destinations. A lot of empty houses in the market now and local businesses serving then closing. 

Then the luxury villas business with the nominee stakeholders. That is what real Thai lawyers recommended so it was the de facto law of the land for decades. Again, ruined. Today, they are in the process of ruining the bustling cannabis business. And with the recent e-visas they are demanding personal bank statements from previous months and daily detailed itineraries. Just for being a 60 day tourist. Again, ruining it! The cancellation wave this winter is going to be epic.
